title: How Much Does Kitchen Fitting Cost UK?
description: How much does kitchen fitting cost UK? Learn typical labour prices, what installation includes, key cost factors and how to budget accurately for your project.
keywords: how much does a new kitchen cost
targetKeyword: how much does kitchen fitting cost uk

blocks.text: If you are researching how much kitchen fitting costs in the UK, the first thing to know is that there is no single standard price. A straightforward installation may cost a few thousand pounds in labour, while a complete kitchen renovation involving new services, flooring, tiling and structural changes can cost considerably more. The final figure depends on the size of the room, the kitchen you choose, the condition of the existing space and how much work is included. As a rough guide, fitting labour for a typical kitchen may be around £2,000 to £6,000, excluding units and appliances. More complex projects can cost more. Every project differs, so obtain a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.
Typical kitchen fitting costs in the UK

Kitchen fitting usually refers to the labour required to install the units, worktops and associated components. As a rough guide, fitting labour for a small or simple kitchen where the existing layout and services stay broadly the same may typically be around £1,500 to £3,000. A medium-sized kitchen with more cabinets, worktop joints and additional trades may typically be around £3,000 to £6,000. A large, bespoke or complicated installation may cost £6,000 to £10,000 or more. These are broad, indicative UK ranges rather than fixed prices; regional labour rates, access, project complexity and the contractor’s scope all make a difference. Every project differs, so request a free quote for accurate pricing.

items: As a rough guide, fitting-only labour for many standard UK kitchens may typically be around £1,500–£6,000, depending on size and complexity.
As a rough guide, a complete new kitchen including units, worktops, appliances and installation may typically cost around £8,000–£25,000 or more.
A premium or bespoke kitchen with specialist worktops, high-end appliances or major building work may cost substantially more.
A kitchen refresh involving replacement doors, worktops or appliances may cost less than a full strip-out and refit. Every project differs, so get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

What is included in kitchen installation?

A kitchen fitting quotation should clearly state which tasks are included and which are priced separately. Standard installation may cover assembling and securing base and wall units, fitting plinths and panels, installing handles, fitting worktops and making cut-outs for sinks or hobs where appropriate. It may also include hanging doors, fitting drawers and connecting some appliances. However, appliance connections, waste removal, decorating and alterations to plumbing or electrics are not always included in a basic fitting price.

items: Removing and disposing of the old kitchen, flooring, wall tiles and unwanted appliances.
Moving water, waste, gas or electrical points to suit a new layout.
Installing or upgrading sockets, lighting, extraction and appliance supplies.
Plastering, making good walls, painting and decorating after the old units are removed.
Fitting wall and floor tiles, vinyl, laminate, timber or other flooring.
Connecting appliances, sinks, taps and waste systems, subject to the installer’s scope and the qualifications required for the work.
Cutting and fitting specialist worktops such as quartz, granite or solid wood.
Repairing damp, uneven floors, damaged plaster or other problems found behind the existing kitchen.

blocks.text: The main factors affecting kitchen fitting cost

The number of units is only one part of the calculation. A quote is also influenced by the condition of the room, the number of trades involved and the precision required for the materials selected. Keeping the existing layout can reduce labour because water, waste and electrical points may not need to move. Changing the position of the sink, cooker or dishwasher often adds time and may require several trades.

items: Room size and layout: larger kitchens need more units, longer worktops and additional installation time.
Kitchen style: flat-pack units may have different labour requirements from rigid, bespoke or hand-painted cabinetry.
Worktops: laminate is generally simpler to install, while stone and other heavy materials may require accurate templating and specialist fitting.
Appliances: integrated appliances, built-in extraction and complex plumbing can take longer than freestanding alternatives.
Services: moving gas, water, waste or electrical supplies can increase both labour and materials costs.
Walls and floors: uneven surfaces, old plaster, damaged flooring or damp may need correcting before installation.
Access: narrow hallways, upper-floor rooms, parking restrictions and limited storage can affect delivery and labour time.
Finishing work: tiling, splashbacks, painting, flooring, lighting and decorating can form a significant part of the overall budget.

blocks.text: How to budget accurately for a kitchen refit

Start by deciding whether you need fitting only, a full replacement kitchen or a wider renovation. Ask suppliers and installers to separate units, worktops, appliances, labour and finishing work, rather than accepting one unexplained total. This makes it easier to compare like-for-like quotations and identify items you may have assumed were included.

items: Measure the room carefully, but arrange a site survey before relying on measurements for ordering.
List every appliance and decide whether it will be freestanding or integrated.
Confirm the worktop material, sink, tap, handles, splashback and storage accessories.
Allow for removal, delivery, waste disposal and any temporary cooking arrangements.
Ask whether plumbing, electrical work, tiling, flooring, plastering and decorating are included.
Include a contingency for unexpected work, particularly in older properties. Every project is different, and hidden defects cannot always be identified before strip-out.
Check the payment schedule, estimated duration, responsibility for ordering materials and process for approving variations.

blocks.text: The most useful quotation is detailed enough for you to understand what will happen from removal through to final clean-up. It should describe the proposed layout, materials, preparation work, installation tasks and exclusions. Be cautious of comparing a low fitting price with a comprehensive quote that includes several trades. A cheaper figure may leave you paying separately for old kitchen removal, appliance connections, tile removal, flooring or making good.

Ways to control the cost without compromising the result

If the budget is tight, keeping the existing layout is often one of the most effective ways to reduce labour. You could also compare worktop materials, retain sound appliances, replace doors rather than every cabinet and phase decorative improvements. However, avoid cutting costs by overlooking preparation or essential electrical and plumbing work. A well-fitted kitchen relies on accurate levelling, suitable support, safe connections and adequate ventilation, so the cheapest initial quote is not necessarily the lowest overall cost.

Before work begins, agree the design, product specifications, schedule and quotation in writing. Confirm who orders the units and appliances, who checks deliveries for damage, and how changes will be priced. Taking these steps gives you a more realistic kitchen fitting budget and reduces the chance of unexpected costs during installation.

faq.q: How much does kitchen fitting cost in the UK?
faq.a: As a rough guide, fitting labour for a typical kitchen may cost around £2,000 to £6,000, excluding units, worktops and appliances. Small or simple installations may cost less, while complex projects can cost more. Every project differs, so get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

faq.q: How much does it cost to fit a kitchen from B&Q or IKEA?
faq.a: The fitting cost depends on the number of units, room preparation, worktops, appliances and service alterations. A supplier’s installation price may not include every plumbing, electrical, tiling or decorating task, so check the scope carefully.

faq.q: Does kitchen fitting include plumbing and electrics?
faq.a: Not always. Some installers may include basic connections, but moving water, waste, gas or electrical points can be priced separately. Ask for each trade and task to be listed clearly in the quotation.

faq.q: How long does it take to fit a kitchen?
faq.a: The duration varies with the size of the kitchen, room preparation, deliveries and the number of trades involved. A straightforward installation may be completed more quickly than a full renovation involving structural work, new services, tiling or flooring.

faq.q: How can I reduce the cost of a kitchen refit?
faq.a: Keeping the existing layout, comparing materials, retaining suitable appliances and avoiding unnecessary structural changes can reduce costs. Do not omit essential preparation, safe connections or ventilation to save money.
